mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the risk-free rate, increasing the present value of equity cash flows and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is continuously observed and the relationship holds for the entire range of observed values.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 1.8%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and residential sales (RSAFS) over the past 3 months signals an impending economic slowdown, prompting the Federal Reserve to adopt a more accommodative monetary policy. This leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline > 2% in 3 months
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS both decline by more than 2% in 3 months, the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment is below 3.5% (UNRATE < 3.5%), the labor market is tight, leading to inflationary pressures and a subsequent monetary tightening cycle that results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE is below 3.5%, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates a strong housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion. This leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy continues to grow.
failure_condition: When HOUST is above 1300, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 in the past month signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to weakening economic activity.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is below 105.0, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 255.0 and a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.0% signals an inflationary shock and a tightening monetary policy. This leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 255.0 and FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0%, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high industrial production regime (INDPRO > 110.0), the manufacturing sector is expanding strongly, which is a leading indicator of economic growth. This leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy continues to expand.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is above 110.0, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
